summary.en: An EU prize for women founders, with a Rising Innovators category for women under 35 (prizes up to €50,000). It is open to founders based in Horizon Europe associated countries, including Georgia, Armenia, Moldova and Ukraine.

summary.ar: جائزة أوروبية لرائدات الأعمال المؤسِّسات، تضم فئة "المبتكرات الصاعدات" للنساء دون 35 عامًا (جوائز تصل إلى 50 ألف يورو). مفتوحة للمؤسِّسات في الدول المنتسبة لبرنامج Horizon Europe ومنها جورجيا وأرمينيا ومولدوفا وأوكرانيا.

about.en:
The European Prize for Women Innovators is jointly awarded by the European Innovation Council and the European Institute of Innovation and Technology. It celebrates women who founded or co-founded innovative companies and turned ideas into real products and services.

In 2027 there are three categories: Women Innovators (€100,000 / €70,000 / €50,000), Rising Innovators for women under 35 (€50,000 / €30,000 / €20,000) and EIT Women Leadership. Applicants must legally reside in an EU Member State or a Horizon Europe associated country, which explicitly includes Georgia, Armenia, Moldova and Ukraine, and their company must be established there.

Beyond the money, finalists get Europe-wide visibility and an award ceremony in the second quarter of 2027. Young founders should look at the Rising Innovators category.

en: Rising Innovators: up to €50,000 for women under 35
Explicitly open to founders in Georgia
Europe-wide visibility for finalists

eligibility.en: Women applying as natural persons, legally resident in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe associated country (incl. Georgia); founder or co-founder of an innovative company established in one of those countries. Rising Innovators: under 35. See the Rules of the Contest.

en: Read the Rules of the Contest on the EIT/EIC page
Choose your category (Rising Innovators if under 35)
Apply through the EU Funding & Tenders portal before 1 Dec 2026, 17:00 CET

costs.en: Free to apply. Prizes from €20,000 to €100,000.

score_reason: Large prize explicitly open to Georgia; needs an existing company

summary.en: A two-semester, non-degree study and internship programme at Polish universities for young leaders from Georgia and other Eastern Partnership and Central Asian countries. The 2027/28 call opens in December 2026 and closes on 1 March 2027.
summary.ka: ორსემესტრიანი, არახარისხიანი სწავლისა და სტაჟირების პროგრამა პოლონურ უნივერსიტეტებში საქართველოსა და აღმოსავლეთ პარტნიორობისა და ცენტრალური აზიის სხვა ქვეყნების ახალგაზრდა ლიდერებისთვის. 2027/28 წლის კონკურსი ცხადდება 2026 წლის დეკემბერში და სრულდება 2027 წლის 1 მარტს.
summary.ar: برنامج دراسة وتدريب غير مانح للشهادة لمدة فصلين في جامعات بولندية، موجّه للقادة الشباب من جورجيا ودول الشراكة الشرقية وآسيا الوسطى. تُفتح دورة 2027/28 في ديسمبر 2026 وتُغلق في 1 مارس 2027.

about.en:
The Lane Kirkland Scholarship Program brings young professionals and leaders from Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova, Tajikistan, Ukraine and Uzbekistan to Poland for two semesters of non-degree study at partner universities in Warsaw, Kraków, Lublin and Wrocław. Fellows follow an individual programme, do a professional internship and write a final project they can use back home.

Fields include economics and management, public administration, law, sociology and social psychology, political science and international relations, development policy, environmental protection, security and crisis management. It suits civil servants, lawyers, entrepreneurs, NGO leaders, journalists and academic teachers who plan to return home and apply what they learn.

The competition is announced every December and the deadline is always 1 March; shortlisted candidates are interviewed in March–April and results come by the end of May. Studies can be in Polish or English (B2), but English-track candidates also need basic Polish (A1).

en: Two fully funded semesters at leading Polish universities
Includes a professional internship and a final project
Georgia is an eligible country; deadline 1 March every year

eligibility.en: Citizens and permanent residents of Georgia (or another listed country); Master's degree or equivalent; up to 40 years old; at least 2 years' professional experience; Polish or English at B2 (English-track candidates also need A1 Polish); no foreign scholarship over 6 months in the previous 2 years.

en: Watch for the 2027/28 call in December 2026 on kirkland.edu.pl
Complete the online application form with a study/project plan (4,000–6,000 characters)
Send two reference letters (Polish, English or Russian) and a copy of your Master's diploma by email
Submit by 1 March 2027; shortlisted candidates are interviewed in March–April

costs.en: Scholarship covers study costs and living allowance in Poland for two semesters (see programme terms).

score_reason: Prestigious, fully funded and Georgia-eligible; for graduates under 40

name.ar: مسابقة الخطابة الرابعة باللغة اليابانية في جورجيا (2026)

deadline_note: Official application period 23 Oct – 10 Nov 2026; screening results by email on 20 Nov

summary.en: The Embassy of Japan's annual speech contest for Georgian learners of Japanese, held at Free University of Tbilisi on 28 November 2026. Beginner, intermediate and advanced speakers give a 3-minute memorised speech on Japanese culture and answer the jury's questions.
summary.ka: იაპონიის საელჩოს ყოველწლიური ორატორული კონკურსი იაპონური ენის შემსწავლელი საქართველოს მოქალაქეებისთვის, 2026 წლის 28 ნოემბერს თბილისის თავისუფალ უნივერსიტეტში. დამწყები, საშუალო და მაღალი დონის მონაწილეები ზეპირად წარმოთქვამენ 3-წუთიან სიტყვას იაპონურ კულტურაზე და პასუხობენ ჟიურის კითხვებს.
summary.ar: مسابقة خطابة سنوية تنظمها سفارة اليابان لمتعلّمي اللغة اليابانية من مواطني جورجيا، في جامعة تبليسي الحرة يوم 28 نوفمبر 2026. يلقي المشاركون من المستويات المبتدئة والمتوسطة والمتقدمة خطابًا محفوظًا مدته 3 دقائق عن الثقافة اليابانية ويجيبون عن أسئلة لجنة التحكيم.

about.en:
The Embassy of Japan in Georgia holds its 4th Japanese Language Speech Contest on Saturday 28 November 2026 (11:00–17:30) in the Auditorium Magnum of Free University of Tbilisi. The general theme is Japanese Culture. It gives learners a stage to show what they have achieved and to meet other students of Japanese.

There are three categories, matched to JLPT/JLCAT levels: beginner (N5–N4 / A1–A2), intermediate (N3 / B1) and advanced (N2–N1 / C1). Each category has two set topics; speeches last 3 minutes, must be delivered from memory, and are followed by questions from the jury in Japanese. Judging covers content (40 points), delivery (30) and answers (30). Winners, runners-up and third places receive certificates of commendation, plus "Good Effort" awards across categories.

If many people apply, the embassy screens applications and may reassign categories; results are emailed on 20 November.

en: Free contest run by the Embassy of Japan
Three levels from beginner to advanced
Certificates for top three in each category

eligibility.en: Georgian citizens learning Japanese. In-service Japanese teachers cannot enter. Past winners may only enter a higher category (advanced winners may re-enter advanced). Anyone who studied in Japan for over a year competes in the advanced category.

en: Choose your category and one of its two topics
Write your speech manuscript in Japanese and in Georgian (name at the top)
Fill in the online application form linked on the embassy page and upload the manuscript and any JLPT/JLCAT certificate
Submit by 10 November 2026
Wait for the screening result and category confirmation on 20 November

score_reason: Open now, free, embassy-run; ideal for Japanese learners in Georgia

name.en: Schuman Traineeships at the European Parliament (October 2027 intake)
name.ka: შუმანის სტაჟირება ევროპარლამენტში (2027 წლის ოქტომბრის ნაკადი)
name.ar: تدريب شومان في البرلمان الأوروبي (دفعة أكتوبر 2027)

deadline_note: Official: applications for the 1 October – end-February period are accepted 1–31 May each year

summary.en: Paid five-month traineeships in the European Parliament's Secretariat in Brussels, Luxembourg or Strasbourg. Graduates from EU candidate countries, including Georgia, are eligible; the next window is 1–31 May 2027.
summary.ka: ხუთთვიანი ანაზღაურებადი სტაჟირება ევროპარლამენტის სამდივნოში ბრიუსელში, ლუქსემბურგსა ან სტრასბურგში. მასში მონაწილეობა შეუძლიათ ევროკავშირის კანდიდატი ქვეყნების, მათ შორის საქართველოს, კურსდამთავრებულებს; შემდეგი მიღება 2027 წლის 1–31 მაისს.
summary.ar: تدريب مدفوع لمدة خمسة أشهر في الأمانة العامة للبرلمان الأوروبي في بروكسل أو لوكسمبورغ أو ستراسبورغ. يحق لخريجي الدول المرشحة لعضوية الاتحاد الأوروبي، ومنها جورجيا، التقديم؛ نافذة التقديم القادمة 1–31 مايو 2027.

about.en:
Schuman traineeships are paid five-month placements in the Secretariat of the European Parliament, in Brussels, Luxembourg, Strasbourg or a Liaison Office. Trainees work in fields such as EU internal and external policy, finance, law, translation and multilingualism, communication, administration and IT, and see from inside how EU laws are made.

Applicants must be 18+, hold a full university degree (or, for a few places, a vocational qualification obtained in the EU), and be nationals of an EU Member State or an accession/candidate country, which includes Georgia. Non-EU citizens need very good English, French or German. You may apply for up to three traineeships.

There are two intakes a year: for 1 October – end of February you apply 1–31 May; for 1 March – 31 July you apply 1–31 October. A monthly grant is paid, and trainees with disabilities can receive extra support through a Positive Action Scheme.

en: Paid traineeship inside an EU institution
Open to nationals of EU candidate countries, including Georgia
Wide range of departments: policy, law, communication, IT

eligibility.en: Aged 18+; EU or accession/candidate-country nationality (Georgia qualifies; a few places for other nationalities); full university degree (EQF 6) or, for limited places, an EU vocational qualification; very good English, French or German for non-EU nationals; no more than two months previous work/traineeship in an EU body.

en: Read the Schuman traineeship rules and FAQ on the European Parliament page
Create an account on the EP traineeship application platform
Select up to three traineeship offers and submit between 1 and 31 May 2027
If shortlisted, upload supporting documents (degree, language, criminal record)

costs.en: Paid: monthly grant plus allowances (see the EP "Monthly grant and allowances" document). Travel and living costs are covered by the grant.

score_reason: Prestigious paid EU traineeship open to Georgian graduates; next window May 2027

name.en: Blue Book Traineeship at the European Commission (October 2027 session)
name.ka: Blue Book სტაჟირება ევროკომისიაში (2027 წლის ოქტომბრის სესია)

summary.en: The European Commission's paid five-month traineeship in Brussels and other EU bodies, open to graduates of any nationality, including Georgia. Registration for the October 2027 session runs 15 February – 12 March 2027.
summary.ka: ევროკომისიის ხუთთვიანი ანაზღაურებადი სტაჟირება ბრიუსელსა და ევროკავშირის სხვა უწყებებში, ღიაა ნებისმიერი ქვეყნის, მათ შორის საქართველოს, კურსდამთავრებულებისთვის. 2027 წლის ოქტომბრის სესიაზე რეგისტრაცია 15 თებერვლიდან 12 მარტამდე გრძელდება.
summary.ar: تدريب مدفوع لمدة خمسة أشهر في المفوضية الأوروبية في بروكسل وهيئات أوروبية أخرى، مفتوح لخريجي جميع الجنسيات ومنها جورجيا. التسجيل لدورة أكتوبر 2027 من 15 فبراير حتى 12 مارس 2027.

about.en:
The Blue Book Traineeship Programme places graduates for five paid months in the European Commission, its executive and decentralised agencies, Commissioners' cabinets and the European External Action Service. Trainees get hands-on experience of EU policy-making and administration in a multicultural team.

The programme is open to university graduates of all nationalities, so students from Georgia can apply alongside EU citizens; there are dedicated IT traineeships and a newer strand for graduates of vocational education and training (VET). Selection is competitive: candidates are pre-selected and then recruited by Commission services.

Registration for the October 2027 session opens on 15 February 2027 and closes on 12 March 2027 (10:00 Brussels time). Apply early and make sure your language certificates and degree documents are ready.

en: Paid five-month traineeship in EU institutions
Open to graduates of any nationality, including Georgia
IT and vocational (VET) strands available

eligibility.en: University graduates (or VET graduates for the VET strand) of any nationality; very good knowledge of English, French or German plus another EU language for EU nationals; no previous traineeship or employment in an EU institution over six weeks. Check the full rules on the programme site.

en: Create an EU Login account and read the Blue Book rules
Prepare your degree, transcripts and language evidence
Register online between 15 Feb and 12 Mar 2027 (10:00 Brussels time)
If pre-selected, you may be contacted by Commission services for interviews

costs.en: Paid: trainees receive a monthly grant; travel costs are reimbursed under the programme rules.

score_reason: Well-known paid EU traineeship open to Georgian graduates; window Feb–Mar 2027

about.en:
American Corner Akhaltsikhe is part of the U.S. Embassy in Georgia's network of 20 American Spaces, run in partnership with local libraries (Akhaltsikhe Central Library, 6a Tamar Mephe Street). Corners host English conversation clubs, science and theme clubs, talks by American diplomats and guest speakers on topics such as entrepreneurship and women's empowerment, and offer English-learning materials and computers to learn about the United States.

Activities are free and open to the public; most participants are school and university students. It is also a practical place to hear about U.S. exchange programmes (such as FLEX), EducationUSA advising and other embassy opportunities, and to network with peers for your own projects.

There is no application round: follow the Corner's page for the weekly schedule and sign-up links for individual events.

en: Free English conversation and science clubs
Meet American diplomats and visiting speakers
Hear first about U.S. exchanges and embassy programmes

eligibility.en: Open to everyone; activities are mostly aimed at school and university students. Some clubs are grouped by English level or age.

en: Visit the Corner at Akhaltsikhe Central Library, 6a Tamar Mephe Street or follow its official page
Check the weekly schedule of clubs and events
Register for the activity you want (some events ask for sign-up in advance)

score_reason: Free, local and always available; informal programme rather than a selective opportunity

about.en:
Culture Moves Europe is the European Union's mobility scheme for the cultural and creative sectors, funded by Creative Europe and implemented by the Goethe-Institut. With €25 million for 2025–2028 it supports around 7,000 artists, cultural professionals and hosts to travel abroad, develop international projects and partnerships, learn, and reach new audiences.

The 2026–2027 individual mobility call is open to artists and cultural professionals aged 18+ who are legal residents of a Creative Europe participating country, which includes Georgia, Armenia, Moldova and Ukraine. Eligible fields are architecture, cultural heritage, design and fashion design, literature, music, performing arts and visual arts. You can apply alone or as a group of up to five, and both emerging and established professionals are welcome.

The grant gives €85 per day of project implementation plus a travel allowance, with top-ups for green travel (€400), visas (€120) and children under 18 (€200 each). Applications are evaluated at the end of every month until 30 April 2027.

en: €85 per day plus travel allowance
Open to residents of Georgia and other Creative Europe countries
Rolling call: decisions every month until April 2027

eligibility.en: Artists and cultural professionals aged 18+ legally residing in a Creative Europe participating country (including Georgia, Armenia, Moldova, Ukraine); working in architecture, cultural heritage, design/fashion, literature, music, performing arts or visual arts; project must take place in another Creative Europe country.

en: Read the call guidelines on the Culture Moves Europe page
Define a mobility project (research, collaboration, residency, production) in another Creative Europe country
Apply online via the Goethe-Institut Culture Moves Europe portal
Applications are evaluated at the end of each month; final deadline 30 April 2027, 23:59 CET

costs.en: Free to apply. Grant: €85/day, travel allowance, plus green (€400), visa (€120) and family (€200 per child) top-ups.

about.en:
American Councils for International Education runs the Eurasian Regional Language Program (ERLP) in Tbilisi, an immersive Georgian-language programme taught by native-speaker experts at the American Councils Language Center in Vake. Classes (about 15 contact hours a week) cover phonetics, grammar, conversation, reading and composition, plus topics in Georgian literature, history, politics and media; heritage speakers and complete beginners are both catered for.

Participants live with Georgian host families (private room, two meals a day), meet regular conversation partners, join weekly cultural activities and regional excursions, and can add internships or volunteering. Academic credit is issued through Bryn Mawr College. The programme is self-funded, with financial aid available, and is aimed mainly at students from the United States, but the page sets no citizenship limit beyond being 18+.

The summer 2027 session runs from 3 June to 1 August 2027 and costs US$7,400 (plus a $45 application fee and a $1,000 deposit counted towards the total). Summer participants can study Georgian, Armenian, Azerbaijani or Russian with no prior study required, and earn 8 undergraduate or 10 graduate credits. Apply by 15 February 2027.

en: Homestay with a Georgian family and weekly excursions
Beginner to advanced levels; credit via Bryn Mawr College
Financial aid available

eligibility.en: Undergraduates, graduates and professionals aged 18+ by the deadline. Summer: no prior language study required for the regional-language option.

about.en:
American Councils for International Education runs the Eurasian Regional Language Program (ERLP) in Tbilisi, an immersive Georgian-language programme taught by native-speaker experts at the American Councils Language Center in Vake. Classes (about 15 contact hours a week) cover phonetics, grammar, conversation, reading and composition, plus topics in Georgian literature, history, politics and media; heritage speakers and complete beginners are both catered for.

Participants live with Georgian host families (private room, two meals a day), meet regular conversation partners, join weekly cultural activities and regional excursions, and can add internships or volunteering. Academic credit is issued through Bryn Mawr College. The programme is self-funded, with financial aid available, and is aimed mainly at students from the United States, but the page sets no citizenship limit beyond being 18+.

The fall 2027 semester runs 24 August – 11 December 2027 (US$16,400) and the academic year runs to 14 May 2028 (US$29,900). about.en:
The DAAD University Summer Courses programme funds students and graduates to deepen their German (general and subject-specific language) and their knowledge of Germany through a four-week summer course at a German university or higher-education institution. Courses run between June and September, with at least 25 teaching hours per week, in person only and taught in German.

The grant covers the course fee, accommodation arranged by the course provider (single room in a dorm, shared flat or private household), a one-time allowance of €475, a country-specific travel allowance, and health, accident and liability insurance. It can only be received once.

Students in Georgia apply directly through the DAAD portal: applications open on 1 September and close on 30 October each year. The 2026 round has just closed, so the next opportunity is the autumn 2027 call for summer 2028 courses. Use the year to reach at least A2 German and get a certificate (Goethe, TestDaF, onSET, telc, ÖSD, DSD).

en: Course fee, accommodation and €475 allowance covered
Travel allowance and insurance included
Wide choice of university summer courses across Germany

eligibility.en: Students and graduates of any subject enrolled at a university in an eligible country such as Georgia (not Germany), aged 18+ at course start; Bachelor's students must have completed at least two years of study; final-year students only if they plan postgraduate study; German at least A2 with a recent certificate.

en: Pick a course from the DAAD summer-course list (Excel/PDF on the DAAD page)
Prepare a CV and motivation letter in German, transcripts and a German certificate (min. A2)
Apply in the DAAD portal between 1 September and 30 October 2027
Wait for the selection committee decision (academic record and motivation are key)

costs.en: Fully funded: course fees, accommodation, €475 allowance, travel subsidy and insurance.

score_reason: Fully funded and open to Georgian students, but next deadline is October 2027

about.en:
The Grant Programme of the Foundation of the Berlin House of Representatives brings outstanding young researchers in any subject to Berlin for almost a full year. It is open to applicants from the United States, the United Kingdom, France and the successor states of the Soviet Union, which includes Georgia. Projects should concern Berlin, German issues or Germany's international relations, or require access to Berlin's research institutions.

About 15 grants are awarded each year for 10 months: €1,100 per month for pre-doctoral students and €1,630 per month for post-doctoral researchers, plus a fixed travel allowance (€200 within Europe, €600 from outside Europe). Grant holders take part in Berlin's academic life and get to know the city's culture and people.

Candidates need at least a first degree, a detailed research plan and a written commitment from a Berlin professor or research-institute director to supervise them. Researchers should be no older than 35 and students generally no older than 25. The deadline is 15 December each year.

en: Ten months in Berlin with a monthly grant
Explicitly open to researchers from Georgia and other post-Soviet states
Small cohort (~15) gives real access to Berlin institutions

eligibility.en: Young researchers of excellent academic merit from the US, UK, France or a post-Soviet state (incl. Georgia); at least a first degree; researchers max. 35, students generally max. 25; research on Berlin/German topics or needing Berlin institutions; confirmed Berlin supervisor.

en: Secure a supervision commitment from a professor or institute director in Berlin
Write a detailed research plan
Download the application forms from the Foundation's page linked in the DAAD database
Submit by 15 December 2026

costs.en: Grant: €1,100/month (pre-doctoral) or €1,630/month (post-doctoral) for 10 months plus €200–600 travel allowance.

score_reason: Georgia-eligible funded research stay, deadline 15 Dec; needs a Berlin supervisor
